newsitem.title: USA: Ill. GOP Sens seen rethinking Chicago airport deal.
newsitem.headline: Ill. GOP Sens seen rethinking Chicago airport deal.

text.p: Illinois Republican state Senators are reconsidering whether they should honor their agreement with Chicago and repeal legislation providing for a state takeover of a lakefront commuter airport, the Chicago Tribune reported Tuesday.

As part of a state and city agreement in January to resolve the dispute over Meigs Field, Chicago officials agreed to keep the airport open for five more years and state officials agreed to repeal a law allowing them to seize the airport before its demolition.
The city reopened the airport, used mainly by business and state aircraft, and plans to turn it into a $27 million bond-financed nature park at the end of the agreement.

Senate President James "Pate" Philip told the Tribune that he has heard the city is not living up to its end of the bargain, including instrument improvements to make Meigs less vulnerable to weather closings.
A city aviation department spokesman said, however, that Chicago has spent $325,000 on improvements at Meigs, the newspaper said.
